Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 26-year-old with known asthma; 2–3 days of increased wheeze, dry cough, shortness of breath beginning during a run and now with brisk walking.  
• Minimal response to salbutamol; preventer taken but may be under-dosed.  
• No fever, sputum, chest pain, or hospitalisations; last asthma attack 3–4 years ago; last asthma review 2 years ago.  

Working diagnosis  
• Asthma exacerbation (loss of control), likely triggered by exercise or allergen – high likelihood supported by history of asthma, wheeze, reduced exercise tolerance, and increased reliever need.

Considerations (medium likelihood)  
• Viral URTI–induced bronchospasm.  
• Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction or poor inhaler technique.

Management  
• Increase Clenil to 4 puffs BID.  
• Salbutamol up to every 2 hours PRN; seek emergency care if needing reliever that frequently or if symptoms worsen.  
• Book face-to-face GP review within a few days for chest exam, peak-flow assessment, and consideration of oral steroids/antibiotics.  
• Provide/refresh written asthma action plan and review inhaler technique at visit.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Asthma exacerbation – High. Established asthma with acute increase in wheeze/SOB and inadequate response to reliever inhaler.  
2. Viral upper respiratory tract infection triggering asthma – Medium. Abrupt onset over days; common precipitant though no systemic viral features.  
3. Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction / poor inhaler technique – Medium. Symptoms started during exercise; prior good control; may coexist.
